# Membership lifecycle

Keep the operator, its roles, and an independent recovery administrator outside managed resources. The recovery administrator needs a user-assignable role with `can_update_all_settings = true` and a working login. Safety checks cannot test recovery access. Terraform does not manage passwords or invitation tokens.

## Declare members

Use `for_each` with email keys and role IDs. Reference managed roles directly for ordering; look up built-in roles or roles managed elsewhere. Only declared emails are managed. Removing an entry removes its access.

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    twenty = {
      source = "glitchedmob/twenty"
    }
  }
}

# Set TWENTY_EMAIL and TWENTY_PASSWORD in the environment.
provider "twenty" {
  endpoint = "https://twenty.example.com"
}

data "twenty_role" "member" {
  label = "Member"
}

resource "twenty_role" "triage" {
  label                       = "Support triage"
  can_be_assigned_to_users    = true
  can_read_all_object_records = true
  permission_flags            = []
}

# Exclude the operator and independent recovery administrator.
resource "twenty_workspace_member" "declared" {
  for_each = {
    "alice@example.com" = twenty_role.triage.id
    "bob@example.com"   = data.twenty_role.member.id
  }
  email   = each.key
  role_id = each.value
}
```

Replace the example emails. Set `TWENTY_EMAIL` and `TWENTY_PASSWORD` in the environment; keep credentials, state, and saved plans private. See [authentication](authentication.md) and the [resource reference](../resources/workspace_member.md) for permissions, lifecycle, and import.

## Recover uncertain access

An ambiguous invitation send, external replacement, or acceptance first observed after cancellation can leave `ownership_confirmed = false`. Refresh alone cannot confirm ownership, and further changes are blocked. There is no automatic retry or rollback; revocation may already have succeeded even if the operation failed.

1. Restore connectivity or permissions, then inspect actual access in Twenty and refresh Terraform state. If complete reads prove access is absent, refresh removes the binding; review the plan before creating again.
2. If access remains unconfirmed, match its current role in configuration. Remove only the local binding and import the existing access:

   ```shell
   terraform state rm 'twenty_workspace_member.declared["alice@example.com"]'
   terraform import 'twenty_workspace_member.declared["alice@example.com"]' '77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777/alice@example.com'
   ```

3. Review the next plan before applying. These state commands do not revoke access. If ownership is still confirmed, fix the reported problem and review the plan without reimporting.

Pause other IAM writers, Terraform runs, and provider aliases during apply. The provider lock covers only one provider configuration; Twenty does not make these changes transactional.

## Before removing accepted members

Twenty can transfer connected accounts and eligible record-share grants to a custodian, make workflow ownership and grants workspace-visible, and delete the member's agent chat history. Removing a user's last workspace also soft-deletes their global user. Treat removal as a data-retention change, not just an access change. Reimporting or restoring membership does not undo these effects.
